notes:
Research: Kaoru Ishikawa, Kawasaki shipyards, 1960s. The six 6M categories are structural scaffolding per SPEC 3: provenance "schema", no quote/confidence/rationale, excluded from the fact/derived counts, and the registry already marks the slot structural.
Edge provenance decision: belongs_to (cause to category) and the category-to-effect spine edges are provenance "schema" - they are the bones of the fish, not claims about the world, so they stay visible when derived is hidden and the fishbone survives the facts-only view. The 6M filing of a specific cause is a judgment; where it is genuinely contestable (the TBPN 'no public corpus' cause reads as Measurements but could be filed as Materials, and 'no lot traceability' in the classic comes from a purchasing sentence but is a records failure) the judgment is discussed in the README rather than hidden in an edge confidence. Recorded here so a later reviewer does not read the schema edges as a provenance claim.
Scout returned three candidates; picked #1 (Chris Power / Hadrian) because it is the only one that populates all six ribs from a single speaker, and it sits in Ishikawa's home domain of manufacturing. Rejected #2 (Mike Gallagher on Navy shipbuilding, Materials rib empty) and #3 (Air India 787 crash, Materials empty and Machines thin).
Empty-rib demonstration: the TBPN source fills all six ribs with facts, so the 'a rib can be empty' lesson is carried by the classic example instead - the minutes end with 'Nobody from maintenance attended the circle, and the mould tool was not discussed', so the Machines rib holds exactly one derived node (c_machines_tool, 0.5). With derived hidden, that bone is visibly bare, which is the diagnostic Ishikawa exists to produce.
Provenance shape: this framework is extraction-heavy. Facts dominate (classic 9/4, tbpn 13/5) because a fishbone's causes are usually said out loud; the inference concentrates at the sub-cause tips, which is why idea_bearing_slot is "subcause".
Validate: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
